MEETCAPPY

Your little privacy companion. A wearable that sniffs out nearby smart glasses and gets mad on your behalf.

CAP (short for Catch a Pervert) is a wearable privacy focused device that is constantly looking out for smart glasses users around you. Cappy is the cute companion living inside of it, reacting to the glasses with expressive eyes and haptic feedback.

01 / THE CONCEPT

Pushing back on Perverts

Camera-equipped smart glasses make recording strangers effortless. I wanted to give the people around them a say.

There’s very little room to consent, or even notice a camera, when it looks like an ordinary pair of glasses. CAP is my response to that imbalance: a wearable device at the intersection of tech and fashion made to combat other wearables that don't respect your privacy.

CAP scans Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) advertisements to look for smart-glasses identifiers. When CAP finds a matching signal, Cappy reacts on its screen and the wearable buzzes, giving you the freedom to decide how to respond to the situation.

Cappy is looking for the presence of camera wearables; a Bluetooth match doesn’t tell me whether their camera is recording or not.

My snap-fit, two-piece printed shell supports the screen and leaves room for the on/off switch and USB-C port.

01

THE ENCLOSURE

A squircle around a circle

I designed CAP’s orange shell in Fusion 360. The two 3D-printed halves snap together around internal screen supports, with a dedicated slot for the on/off switch and access to the USB-C port.

3D-PRINTED SHELL · SNAP-FIT · USB-C ACCESS

02

THE DISPLAY

Cappy’s expressive face

Cappy lives on CAP’s 1.28-inch round TFT LCD, which gives him his eyes. LovyanGFX renders the blinks, glances, and state changes at around 30 frames per second, making the face feel alive between alerts.

GC9A01 · 240 × 240 PX · SPI · 30 FPS

Try his expressions ↓
03

THE BRAIN

Listening for smart glasses

The compact ESP32-S3-Zero runs continuous NimBLE advertisement scans and looks for manufacturer IDs and device names matching with popular smart glasses like the Meta Raybans, then smooth the RSSI readings to move Cappy through his proximity tiers and expressions without flickering between states.

ESP32-S3-ZERO · NimBLE · SMOOTHED RSSI

Inside CAP’s firmware ↗
04

KNOCKS & BUZZES

Alerts you can feel

I configured an ADXL345 accelerometer as a physical knock detector: two knocks wake Cappy from a nap. A vibration motor gives single, double, or triple buzzes as the alert escalates, so you can respond without looking at his face when you are wearing the device.

ADXL345 · DOUBLE-KNOCK · MOSFET MOTOR DRIVER

━━ ━━ ━ ━
05

BATTERY & CHARGING

Ready to come along

A 3.7V LiPo battery and TP4056 USB-C charging circuit power the wearable. I soldered the connections into a self-contained unit, with a physical switch on the side to turn CAP on and off.

3.7V LiPo · TP4056 · USB-C · ON/OFF SWITCH

03 / MEET CAPPY

Cappy's Emotions

Cappy brings CAP’s alerts to life through his expressive eyes. Let's take a look at his range of emotions.

  1. HAPPY

    The coast is clear

    His default state: white eyes looking around, with no alerts to worry about.

    No vibration
  2. CURIOUS

    Something nearby

    A matching BLE signal catches his attention. His eyes turn yellow.

    One short vibration
  3. ANGRY

    Getting too close

    Someone wearing smart glasses is getting closer. Red eyes make his objection clear.

    Two vibrations
  4. RAGE

    Personal space, please

    They’ve ignored the warning and moved right in. His screen flashes red.

    Three vibrations
  5. SLEEPY

    Time for a nap

    After 30 seconds of quiet, his eyes droop and he gets sleepy.

    Double-knock to wake
  6. SLEEPING

    Sound asleep

    At 60 seconds of quiet, his eyes close and the Zs float up. Double-knock CAP to wake him, a little groggy.

    Double-knock to wake

I’ve recreated Cappy’s reactions here so you can try them in your browser. Drag the glasses closer to see how he responds, then let him doze off and knock twice to wake him.

04 / IN THE WILD

CAPPY, out in the world

WAYS TO WEAR

Wear Cappy your way

Cappy is built around freedom and choice. Your shirt and waistband are just two possibilities that I tested. You’re free to wear it however you want, and choose how visible you want to be.

OUT IN THE OPEN

On your shirt

Let people meet Cappy. His reactions can start a conversation about recording, consent, and the person behind the lens.

JUST BETWEEN YOU TWO

On your waistband

Clip CAP discreetly to your pants and feel the vibration alerts privately. You choose whether to confront an onlooker.

THE CLASS DEMO

Cappy meets the class

For the live class demo, My classmate wore our improvised “unreleased” glasses while carrying my bluetooth earphones (added to CAP’s target list to test Cappy without the glasses) to trigger real-time BLE detection. I showed Cappy’s changing expressions, CAP’s vibration alerts, and the double-knock interaction that wakes him on stage.
